name: Rizpah
overview: Rizpah, a concubine of Saul, is remembered in Scripture for her profound devotion and mourning over the deaths of her sons, who were executed by hanging at King David's command as part of a covenant with the Gibeonites. Her steadfast vigil, as she spread sackcloth and guarded their bodies from scavengers from the beginning of the barley harvest until rain fell, highlights a poignant example of loyal love and grief amid divine judgment. This narrative underscores the human cost of national sin and the faithfulness of an individual amidst tragedy.
